# Nehemiah Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 471r–471v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_004_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** When Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was furious and greatly angered, and he mocked the Jews.

**2** He said before his brothers and the army of Samaria, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore things? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they revive the stones from the heaps of burned rubble?"

**3** Tobiah the Ammonite, beside him, said, "Even what they are building — if a fox goes up on it, he will break down their stone wall!"

**4** Hear, O our God, for we are despised. Turn their reproach back on their own heads. Give them over as plunder in a land of captivity.

**5** Do not cover over their guilt, and do not let their sin be blotted out from your sight, for they have provoked you before the builders.

**6** So we built the wall, and the entire wall was joined to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.

**7** But when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of Jerusalem's walls was advancing and the breaches were beginning to be closed, they were very angry.

**8** They all conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to cause confusion in it.

**9** We prayed to our God and set a guard against them day and night.

**10** But in Judah it was said, "The strength of the burden-bearers is failing, and there is too much rubble. We cannot rebuild the wall."

**11** Our adversaries said, "They will not know or see until we come into their midst and kill them and stop the work."

**12** The Jews who lived near them came and told us ten times, "From every direction they will come against us."

**13** So I stationed men at the lowest points behind the wall, in the exposed places. I stationed the people by their clans with their swords, spears, and bows.

**14** I looked and arose and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your homes."

**15** When our enemies heard that their plan was known to us and that God had frustrated it, we all returned to the wall, each to his work.

**16** From that day on, half of my men worked at construction while half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The officers stood behind the whole house of Judah.

**17** Those building the wall and those carrying burdens each worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other.

**18** Each builder had his sword strapped at his side while he built. The man who sounded the trumpet stayed beside me.

**19** I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, "The work is great and spread out, and we are far apart on the wall from one another.

**20** Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, rally to us there. Our God will fight for us."

**21** So we pressed on with the work, while half held their spears from the break of dawn until the stars came out.

**22** I also said to the people at that time, "Let every man and his servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so they may guard us by night and work by day."

**23** Neither I nor my brothers nor my servants nor the men of the guard who followed me — none of us took off our clothes. Each kept his weapon at hand.

---

## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Nehemiah 4 dramatizes the intersection of prayer and practical action that defines Nehemiah's leadership. The chapter escalates through mockery (vv. 1-3), conspiracy (vv. 7-8), internal despair (v. 10), and assassination threats (v. 11), yet the response is always the same twofold pattern: pray and act (v. 9). The iconic image of workers with tool in one hand and weapon in the other (v. 17) captures the paradox of building in hostile territory. Nehemiah's rallying cry — "Our God will fight for us" (v. 20) — deliberately echoes holy war tradition, recasting wall construction as a continuation of God's ancient deliverance.

---

## Disagreement Log

### V.2 — "feeble" vs. "pathetic" vs. "weak"
- **EMET:** "feeble" (*ha-amelallim*) / **LOGOS:** "feeble" / **PNEUMA:** "pathetic"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "feeble" — The Hebrew *amelal* means withered or feeble; "pathetic" (PNEUMA) imports too much modern contempt. "Feeble" accurately conveys the physical weakness implied.

### V.6 — "had a mind to work" vs. "had a heart to work" vs. "were determined to work"
- **EMET:** "had a-heart to-work" / **LOGOS:** "had a mind to work" / **PNEUMA:** "were determined to work"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "had a heart to work" — The Hebrew uses *lev* (heart), the seat of will and intention in Hebrew anthropology. "Mind" (LOGOS) shifts to a Western cognitive frame; "determined" (PNEUMA) loses the embodied Hebrew idiom.

### V.23 — textual difficulty in final clause
- **EMET:** "each his-weapon and the-water" / **LOGOS:** "each kept his weapon at hand" / **PNEUMA:** "we kept our weapons with us at all times"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "each kept his weapon at hand" — The Hebrew *shilcho ha-mayim* is textually obscure. LOGOS's rendering captures the clear sense of constant readiness without forcing the corrupted text.

---

*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
